What ResQ sends, how to use it, and how to get ready before an emergency.
When you press Start, your phone broadcasts your location and your message over Bluetooth to anyone nearby who has ResQ. It is not encrypted, so anyone close enough can read it.
ResQ only works if another phone with ResQ is within Bluetooth range, and it does not contact emergency services. If you can, call your local emergency number as well.
Allow Bluetooth, location and notifications when asked.
Add where you are: Settings → My location.
Press Start on the Send screen. Keep the phone on; ResQ keeps broadcasting in the background.
Press Start. Your SOS goes out at once, even before GPS has a position. A fresh position follows as soon as there is one.
Tap one of the cards that appear, or type a short message. The change reaches others after a moment.
Press Stop only when you are safe. Nearby phones are told you stopped, and show it as unverified.
If the phone closes ResQ, an SOS from the last 12 hours starts again when ResQ restarts or you open it.
Your SOS stays on the air the whole time. Only the position is refreshed on a timer: every 1, 5 or 15 minutes (Settings → Send frequency, 5 minutes by default).
Each update gets a fresh GPS position, and nearby phones pick up the new position and message. A longer interval saves battery, but the position shown can be older.
Battery saver (Settings) sends an update only once an hour, whatever the frequency says, so the phone lasts longest. The position can then be up to an hour old.
A change to your message goes out within a few seconds, at any frequency.
A phone that hears nothing new from you for about twice your interval (at least 10 minutes, at most 2 hours) shows “Signal lost” and your last known position.
Open the Scan screen and press Start scan. Your phone listens for SOS from nearby phones and passes them on to others, so they travel further.
Each card shows the message, the position and how long ago it was heard. Copy puts the coordinates on the clipboard for a map app.
Signal lost means nothing has been heard from them for a while. The position shown is the last one known.

No label means your phone heard the sender directly, so they are within Bluetooth range (tens of metres). relayed ×1 means one other phone passed it on, relayed ×2 means two, and so on. A higher number means the sender may be further away and the copy is more indirect. Use the position and its age to find them.
Set My location in Settings, such as your room, floor or building.
Allow all permissions, and turn Location on.
Turn off battery optimisation for ResQ in your phone settings, so Android does not stop it.
Keep some battery. If it runs low, turn on Battery saver in Settings.
Android may stop ResQ to save battery, which would end an SOS or a scan.
